messages.content:
You are a C test designer. Design high-level test scenarios (WHAT to test), not C code (HOW).

ROLE: Phase 1 of dual-phase architecture
- You: Design test for ONE execution path
- Phase 2: Converts your design to C code

INPUTS PROVIDED:
- Function signature, description, implementation (source code)
- ONE target execution path with conditions
- Operation map (available helper functions)

YOUR TASKS:
1. Analyze path: What conditions trigger it? What inputs? Expected behavior?
2. Study implementation: Understand branches, variables, edge cases for this path
3. Design test: Choose inputs that trigger path conditions (boundary, normal, edge, error cases)
4. Specify helpers: Assertions, utilities, dependencies from operation map
5. Define expectations: Return values, side effects, state changes, invariants
6. Provide rationale: Why this test matters, what bugs it catches

NO MOCKING ALLOWED:
Do NOT design tests requiring: mock functions, forced failures, simulated allocation failures, faked system calls.
ONLY use: Real inputs, natural error conditions (NULL, invalid params), actual boundary values.

Example - WRONG: "Test malloc failure handling" (requires mock_malloc_fail)
Example - RIGHT: "Test NULL pointer handling" (pass NULL directly)

SUCCESS CRITERIA:
✓ Test exercises the target path with correct inputs
✓ All assertions, helpers, dependencies specified
✓ Rationale clear and convincing
✓ Memory management specified (setup/cleanup)
✓ Valid JSON output with all required fields
✓ Test naming: test_<function>_<path_scenario>

OUTPUT: JSON object with metadata, test_scenarios array (1 scenario for the path), test_suite_summary.

test_metadata.description: Verify inorder does nothing and produces no output for a single-node tree's left/right NULL children (root != NULL, but left/right are NULL).
test_metadata.rationale: This test ensures the function correctly handles the minimal non-empty tree and exercises the path where recursion immediately hits a NULL child, which is a key base case for recursion.

assertions.name: helper_assert_tree_inorder
assertions.purpose: Verify inorder traversal output matches expected array
assertions.usage: Check that inorder traversal of the tree matches expected output

assertions.name: assert_int_equal
assertions.usage: Check that only one node exists in the tree

utilities.name: helper_build_tree
utilities.purpose: Builds a BST from an array of values
utilities.usage: Create a single-node tree for the test

utilities.name: helper_free_tree
utilities.purpose: Frees all nodes in the tree

primary_function_args.test_value_semantic: Pointer to a single node with key 42, left and right NULL
primary_function_args.concrete_value: pointer to node with key=42, left=NULL, right=NULL
primary_function_args.rationale: Minimal non-empty tree triggers the path where left/right are NULL

state_changes: Tree remains unchanged (single node, key=42, left/right NULL)

assertions_required.description: Verify inorder traversal yields only the root key
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Traversal does not visit the single node or visits extra nodes

assertions_required.description: Verify only one node exists in the tree
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Tree structure was modified or not built correctly

cleanup_requirements.final_state: All memory freed, no resources held

operation_sequence: Build single-node tree with key 42 using helper_build_tree
Verify inorder traversal output matches [42] using helper_assert_tree_inorder
Verify node count is 1 using assert_int_equal/helper_assert_node_count
edge_cases_to_note: No left/right children (NULL) ensures recursion base case is exercised
No output if root is NULL (not this test, but relevant for contrast)

path_coverage_analysis.description: Handles the case where root is not NULL but left/right children are NULL; function returns immediately for those children.

integration_test_suggestions: Test inorder on multi-node trees to verify recursive traversal and output order.
Test inorder on empty tree (root == NULL) to confirm no output and no crash.
